remeasured: 2026-10-25, against the gate as of KeePassGate 0.1.0

verdicts.served: PyKeePassGate can implement this today, over routes the gate already serves, with the meaning pykeepass gives it.
verdicts.served-differently: The gate has the operation, but it does something other than pykeepass's member of that name, so a facade must not offer it under that name.
verdicts.needs-routes: Nothing in the design forbids it; the gate does not serve it yet.
verdicts.refused: Cannot exist on this side: it needs the file, the key, the XML document, or an operation the design refuses.

attachments: one GET per entry, so a database wide sweep is O(entries)
deref: pykeepassgate.refs, which compiles a reference on the client's side under the caller's own rules, held to KeePass's own compiler
find_entries: built on the listing and the read routes
find_entries_by_username: needs a read per candidate, so it costs list plus N
trash_entry: DELETE /entries/{uuid}, which sends the entry to the recycle bin when the database keeps one
trash_group: DELETE /groups/{uuid}, for an empty group, the same way
delete_entry: DELETE /entries/{uuid} sends the entry to the recycle bin, where pykeepass's removes it for good, so a facade offers trash_entry and not this
delete_group: DELETE /groups/{uuid} refuses a group that is not empty and sends an empty one to the recycle bin, where pykeepass's removes the group and everything in it for good
recyclebin_group: database metadata the gate does not name; the bin itself stays out of reach
binaries: a database wide binary pool has no node for the ACL to authorize against
credchange_date: key change policy, which lives with the file
empty_group: recursive delete, refused so that one grant cannot destroy entries nobody decided about
move_entry: one operation about two nodes, and the router authorizes one. API.md records the refusal
password: the client never holds the master password, which is the point of the gate
save: the trap this whole question is about: it writes the file it was opened from
xml: there is no XML document on this side

group: read: the entry's group. Setting it is a move, refused like move_entry
otp: a field named otp, which is all pykeepass reads
password: the Password field, under the protected switch
ref: builds a {REF:...} text on the client's side and needs nothing from the gate
title: served
the Title field
delete: DELETE /entries/{uuid} sends the entry to the recycle bin, where pykeepass's removes it for good
atime: the last access time, not served; KeePass moves it whenever an entry is viewed
history: every update keeps a revision, as KeePass does, and no route reads one; a revision holds earlier protected values, so reading it is a question for the protected switch
index: an entry's place among its group's entries, not served
is_a_history_entry: only means something once history is served
reindex: moving an entry within its group, not served
tags: KeePass keeps tags on an entry and the gate neither serves nor writes them
autotype_enabled: auto-type settings would let a client that may update an entry, but not read its password, point auto-type at a window it controls and have KeePass type the password there
delete_history: a revision is what keeps an overwritten value recoverable, and destroying it is left to the operator, as emptying the recycle bin is
dump_xml: there is no XML document on this side
save_history: every update through the gate already keeps a revision, so a method that asks for one would do nothing
touch: the times are KeePass's, moved by the writes that change something; a write that changes nothing writes nothing

group: read: parent. Setting it is a move, refused like move_group
is_root_group: the root is the group addressed as root
name: served
name, read and written
delete: DELETE /groups/{uuid} refuses a group that is not empty, where pykeepass's removes the group and everything in it for good
atime: the last access time, not served
append: puts an entry into this group, which for one already elsewhere is a move
dump_xml: there is no XML document on this side
expires: a group's expiry is neither served nor accepted, API.md records why
touch: the times are KeePass's, moved by the writes that change something

delete: DELETE /entries/{uuid}/attachments/{name}, which takes it off that entry as pykeepass's does
entry: the entry the attachment is addressed through
id: an index into the database wide binary pool, which has no node for the ACL to authorize against
